_placeholders: Placeholder copy (D1013, flavour rule D1015): engineer drafts from the design lore index, every item citing its lore ids; Design signs or edits it (design specs/NEWS_FEED.md). Skill: walklings-lore-feed.
_about: Block News for the NEWS app (news.js). stories, voices, notices, polls, you. Gates: when (story.flag, !story.flag, story.side=keepers|glimmer), sky, phase, me. lead: the front page once eligible, highest wins. Tokens: {holder} {partner} {town} {seals} {steps}. lore: ids in the design repo lore/lore_index.json.

stories.headline: Big morning on the hill: today could be yours
body: Warden Ilse is at the Lodge, and the Keepers give each young holder a Walkling. Today could be your turn.
The sign on the hill keeps it short: 'Hill village of the Keepers. Home.'
Advice from home, free with breakfast: 'A bond grows in small jobs.'

replies.name: Porch sitter
replies.text: Somebody just ran to the Lodge in slippers. Respect.

replies.name: Lane sweeper
replies.text: Swept the Lodge step twice this morning. Big day for somebody.

stories.headline: Three small faces, one very big choice
body: Pipkit (EMBER), Drizzlet (TIDE) and Sproutbun (BLOOM) wait at Warden Ilse's Lodge for their holders.
Ilse's word to every new holder: 'That trust is the only armour you have.' Pick the one that looks back.

replies.name: Schoolhouse kid
replies.text: Team Sproutbun. Look at it. Case closed.

stories.headline: Short on Acorns? The bed is still a bed
body: A Lantern House rest costs 5 Acorns. Got 1-4? Pay what you have. Got none? It's free.
Della keeps Hearthmoor's beds and explains healing to anyone who asks. Ask.
Lose a battle and you wake at the last Lantern House you visited. Plan your naps.

stories.headline: Market Row: bring Acorns, leave lighter
body: Lamplight Provisions, Stitch & Lantern and The Parked Coach line Market Row. Your Acorns will find a use.
Hearthmoor Plaza, the Keepers' square, sits west of home. West watch is on duty.
Lanternball Court and the Schoolhouse round out the hill. One of them is louder. Guess.

stories.headline: Keeper House: say your piece, then step back
body: Two floors, one motto: 'Hearthmoor watch. The lantern's law.' Citizens wait in the doorway.
The Keepers ask every holder to walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them. Feed, rest, listen.
Citizen. Say your piece, then step back. A holder is offered a chair.

stories.headline: Care column: GLOWING has no shortcut
body: Keep care at 75 or more and your Walkling shows the GLOWING mood. No gadget required.
Growing up waits for Lv 12. Until then, as they say at home, a bond grows in small jobs.

stories.headline: East gate opener: you vs. Neighbour Rook
body: The first Neighbour match is done at Hearthmoor's east gate. Rook took the starter that beats yours. Typical.
Rook, Mrs. Calloway's son: competitive, kind underneath. The kind part takes its time.
Officer Cald's gate count is pinned to the town board, for anyone keeping score.

replies.name: Lanternball fan
replies.text: Heard it from the court. Best match on the hill today, and I watch a lot of matches.

replies.name: Hill local
replies.text: Mrs. Calloway watched from the step like it was a parade.

stories.headline: Bell at 8, out at 3, Buddy never late
body: Lizzy teaches 8-3 on weekdays. Pip and Wren hold the front row, mostly upright.
Her Walkling Buddy is a Harvestail and is never wild. Please stop trying to befriend it at the gate.

stories.headline: Route 1: walk slow, the grass is shy
body: Hearthmoor to Fernbrook, one road. Tall grass hides shy Walklings, so step softly.
Officer Ness issues the Keeper1 out here. Say hello before you say anything else.

stories.headline: Your Keeper1 is on. So are the Keepers.
body: Officer Ness hands every holder a free Keeper1. The Keeper High Court mandates one for every holder.
On the network: 'We own the poles from this hill to the coast. There is no other net.'
The small print, in large print: 'Your Keeper1 is active. We can read this. That is the service.'

replies.name: New holder
replies.text: Free phone, zero choice, great signal. Mixed feelings, full bars.

replies.name: Route regular
replies.text: Typed a rude word. Deleted it. Felt watched. Felt kindly watched.

stories.headline: Forecast: the sky is listening
body: The Amberwild's sky listens to the Far Sky. Real weather changes which species stir in the grass.
Dawn 5-7, day 7-18, dusk 18-20, then night. A whole day here passes in 42 real minutes. Blink, it's dusk.

stories.headline: Ribbit rides the wires. Mind your manners.
body: Ribbit, the social feed, rides the Keeper wires. Post freely. Post kindly.
The Keepers are kind and also watching. Wave.

stories.headline: Orchard village says hello (so do the Pomlets)
body: Fernbrook: orchard village, home of the Bloom Trial Hall. Pomlets live in the orchard and act like it.
Keepers keep the town. Glimmerwell keeps a stand. The square has opinions about both.
Keeper Amos hosts the Lantern House: beds, a rest, and a proper explanation.

replies.name: Orchard hand
replies.text: Welcome! Mind the Pomlets. They will not mind you.

replies.name: Square regular
replies.text: New face on the square. The stand smiled first. The orchard took longer.

stories.headline: Free lanterns on the square, one grey Fuzzwick
body: Associate Juniper is handing out free Glimmer lanterns on the square: 'Brighter by nature!'
A grey Fuzzwick sits by the stand. Fuzzwicks love lanterns. This one has lost its colour.
A reminder from the desk: Lantern Houses do not cure Fade. Care does.

replies.name: Orchard hand
replies.text: Took a free lantern. Gave it back. The Fuzzwick watched me the whole time.

stories.headline: Free light, zero forms. You're welcome!
body: Glimmerwell Co. is proud to keep a stand in Fernbrook. Free Glimmer lanterns, no forms, no fuss!
Feeling tired? Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting! Brighter by nature.
It's a partnership! Have a bright day!

stories.headline: Hall Master skips the Hall for the trees
body: Master Fen of the Bloom Trial Hall is out in the orchard, worried about her orchard friends.
Associate Tobin has crates stacked at the orchard gate. Asked why, he points to the memo.

replies.name: Orchard hand
replies.text: Fen checked every tree twice today. The trees looked grateful. The crates did not.

stories.headline: A promise at the gate: the crates come open
body: At the orchard gate a holder stood with Master Fen: 'Roots are a promise.' Then the crates came open.
They were bound for 'the Sanctuary'. Now they are bound for nowhere at all.
Keepers earn Standing from care and kindness. Freeing crated Walklings counts.

replies.name: Orchard hand
replies.text: Saw a crate lid come off. Something small sneezed. Good sign.

replies.name: Lantern House regular
replies.text: Fen smiled. Out loud, almost. Somebody write it down.

stories.headline: New lanyard at the gate. Welcome aboard!
body: A Fernbrook holder took the Junior Bright trial lanyard at the orchard gate. Brighter by nature!
Crates for 'the Sanctuary' are packed with care. Quarterly targets love a team player!
Tiers run Guest, Associate, Junior Bright, Bright Lead. Climb with us. Have a bright day!

replies.name: Square regular
replies.text: The lanyard is very mint. The crates are very quiet.

stories.headline: Pomlets home; blossoms on high alert
body: The orchard crates are empty. Master Fen's orchard friends are back out among the trees.
Pomlet, Pomshell, Orchardon: the whole line is home where it grows. The blossoms have been warned.

replies.name: Orchard hand
replies.text: Found a Pomlet in my lunch basket. Not complaining. Not getting lunch back either.

stories.headline: Orchard units packed, right on target!
body: The Pomlet units are packed at the orchard gate, a shade paler and right on schedule!
Master Fen: 'I hoped your hands would know better.' Feedback is a gift. Have a bright day!

replies.name: Orchard hand
replies.text: The trees are very quiet today. I keep looking up anyway.

stories.headline: 'Wear it kindly': Fernbrook Seal awarded
body: Master Fen awarded the Fernbrook Seal at the Bloom Trial Hall, with three words: 'Wear it kindly.'
One Seal lifts the level cap from 15 to 22. Kindness, it turns out, has levels.

replies.name: Hall usher
replies.text: Swept the Hall after. Found petals and one very proud Walkling.

stories.headline: Tier 1 Lanyard: smile for the wall!
body: The Bright Pavilion Tour ends with a Tier 1 Lanyard, the Bright stand-in for a Seal. Congratulations!
Your photo now hangs beside the Sanctuary crate list. Brighter by nature!

replies.name: Square regular
replies.text: Good photo. Odd frame. The list next to it is long.

stories.headline: Heights: the night crates are open
body: A night smuggling ring moved Walklings through the old tunnels of Fernbrook Heights. Its crates are open.
The broker, Mara Quill, was 'wrong, not cruel'. The tunnels are quiet now.
Fernbrook Heights is a ridge north of Fernbrook: a lab, and old tunnels. Tonight, mostly wind.

replies.name: Ridge walker
replies.text: Walked the tunnels after. Empty. Echoey. Much better.

stories.headline: An Atten vial joins the partnership!
body: RegenX on Fernbrook Heights brews Atten. A copied vial is now safely with the partnership!
The cheap-brew plans are filed 'for the partnership'. Decent people, decent paperwork. Have a bright day!

replies.name: Lab visitor
replies.text: Everyone at the lab is smiling today. Nobody is making eye contact.

stories.headline: Meet the ridge lab of 'decent people'
body: RegenX, the lab on the ridge, is a lab of 'decent people'. Atten is its brew.
On the floor: Nia, Cal and Dr. Ivo. Out on the ridge: clerk Jed. Wave at all of them.

stories.headline: Upstairs at RegenX: a computer that floats
body: RegenX's top bay holds 'a floating computer'. Glimmerwell found it, keeps it, and calls it a 'cradle'.
It emits slowly. The screen is dark.
Quinn, in the bay: 'We do not know what it sends. The old ones built it. That is all I was told.'

replies.name: Bay sweeper
replies.text: I dust around it. It does not need dusting. It floats above the dust.

stories.headline: The cradle hummed. A Bitlet woke up.
body: A Bitlet, a VOLT Walkling, woke in the Arbiter Bay when the cradle hummed.
Staff are firm on one point: 'It is not a product.' The Bitlet seems to agree.

replies.name: Lab visitor
replies.text: It blinked at me. I blinked back. We are friends now, I think.

stories.headline: Route 2 reopens, with a census tent attached
body: The Fernbrook-to-Cobblecrest path is open. "Path reopened by Glimmerwell Co. crews!" says the sign, brightly.
A Glow Census tent stands by the path. Walkers heading east will pass it, like it or not.

replies.name: Route walker
replies.text: Walked past the tent at a totally normal speed. Very normal. No eye contact.

replies.name: Fernbrook walker
replies.text: Path is open. My Walkling already has strong opinions about the gravel.

stories.headline: Route 2 is open. Walk it the Keeper way
body: Glimmerwell Co. crews reopened the path. The Keepers have noted it. The road itself is yours.
Walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them. Feed, rest, listen, and leave glow where it grows.

stories.headline: The Glow Census is in town. Smile, you count!
body: The Glow Census is counting on Route 2. Up in Wickerglen, the Comfort Lamps pulse like a slow heartbeat.
Brighter by nature. It's a partnership! Have a bright day.

stories.headline: Every Census log counts. Yes, even that one
body: Standing grows with output and quotas: befriends, battles won, Census logs, crates packed.
Feeling tired on the road? Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting!

stories.headline: Wickerglen to visitors: please, keep it down
body: The sign reads: "Hush, please. Walklings nap here between the roots." Comfort Lamps glow among them.
We asked Associate Hollis what his lamp does. "I just hold the lamp." He did not elaborate.

replies.name: Glen walker
replies.text: Whispered the whole way through. My Walkling sneezed once. We are both very sorry.

replies.name: Root sitter
replies.text: Those lamps sure are pretty. Pretty what, I'm still deciding.

stories.headline: Lights out in Wickerglen. Colour comes back on
body: The Comfort Lamps in Wickerglen clicked off after a battle with Field Lead Imogen. The glen went quiet.
Colour is coming back to the glen, where a grey Pebblit had been seen. The roots look relieved.

replies.name: Root sitter
replies.text: The moss is greener. I'm not saying it's related. I'm saying it's greener.

replies.name: Glen walker
replies.text: First nap here with no lamp over me. Slept like a stone. Like a Pebblit, really.

stories.headline: Meet the Field Lead keeping Wickerglen aglow
body: The Comfort Lamps collect a little extra glow. Glimmerwell calls it glow sharing. Sharing is lovely!
Field Lead Imogen's word to the team: "Quarterly review, sweetie."

stories.headline: Grey isn't gone: caring for a Faded Walkling
body: A grey Pebblit was seen at Wickerglen. A drained Walkling is Faded, and Lantern Houses do not cure Fade.
Care does. On recovery, colour is back, and it remembers who it is. Be patient. Be kind.

stories.headline: Welcome to Cobblecrest. Mind the Pebblits
body: A quarry town at the far end of Route 2. Please mind the Pebblits underfoot. They will not mind you.
The STONE Trial Hall is Master Hale's. His word: "Forty years I dug beside Walklings."

replies.name: Quarry kid
replies.text: Tripped on a Pebblit. Said sorry to the Pebblit. That's just how it works here.

replies.name: Porch sitter
replies.text: Holders keep rolling in with that long Route 2 look. Sit down. Have some shade.

stories.headline: Brinewick Road: closed. Crates: loading
body: The sign on Cobblecrest's road east: "BRINEWICK ROAD. Closed while crates are loaded."
The sign does not say for how long. Signs rarely do.

stories.headline: Crates head for "the Sanctuary". Keepers watch
body: Glimmerwell's crates of Walklings are bound for "the Sanctuary". The Keepers have taken note.
Citizen: say your piece, then step back. The Keepers are kind, and also watching.

stories.headline: Cobblecrest votes; the quarry goes by three
body: Cobblecrest's quarry was sold by a town vote. It passed by three votes. Three.
The buyer: Glimmerwell Co., via Dorian Pell, Head of Acquisitions. The site is now Bright Quarry.
Reeve Tamsin: "The vote passed fair and square. I only wish it felt fair."

replies.name: Quarry kid
replies.text: Counted the result twice. Still three. Still don't like it.

replies.name: Stone hauler
replies.text: The Acquisitions man calls them units. Mine is a Pebblit with a favourite rock.

stories.headline: Bright Quarry: same stone, brighter future!
body: Bright Quarry, a Glimmerwell Co. site, is open. Clerk Mint is at the desk for all your quarry needs.
It's a partnership! Have a bright day.

stories.headline: Stone cold: a holder takes Hale's Seal
body: A holder has earned Master Hale's Cobblecrest Seal at the Stone Hall. Hale nodded. For Hale, that's a parade.
Two Seals raise the level cap to Lv 30. The next grow-up needs Lv 24 plus 2 Seals.

replies.name: Quarry kid
replies.text: Hale nodded at them. HALE. NODDED. I've waited my whole life for that nod.

replies.name: Porch sitter
replies.text: Higher level cap, they say. My Pebblit is still working on the porch step.

stories.headline: Tier 2 Lanyards are in! Wear yours brightly
body: Congratulations on your Tier 2 Lanyard! Associate Quinn ran your second review.
Some partners hear a soft click afterward. Totally normal. Have a bright day!

replies.name: Junior hopeful
replies.text: A Tier 2 Lanyard looks so good on mint. Mine is still Tier 1. Patience.

replies.name: Crate packer
replies.text: Heard the soft click too. Asked about it. Got a smile and a brochure.

stories.headline: Neighbour Rook steps off the cart
body: Rook, the holder's Neighbour, picked for Junior Bright in spring, got off the cart.
His words: "I am with you, if you will have me." Hearthmoor's porches will be talking for weeks.

replies.name: Porch sitter
replies.text: Always said that boy was kind underneath. Competitive on top. Kind underneath.

stories.headline: Rook re-ups with the company. Bright move!
body: Rook's words: "I am staying with the company." Junior Bright is Rook's level, and he wears it well.
He's a little nervous about what comes next. He wants it anyway. That's the spirit!

replies.name: Crate packer
replies.text: Junior Bright and staying put. Love a team player. Output and quotas, Rook!

stories.headline: Three Pebblits out; Hale opens the seam
body: Three crated Pebblits in Cobblecrest are free, and Master Hale has opened the seam. Lids off, stones warm.
Freeing crated Walklings is care and kindness. The Keepers count it toward Standing.

replies.name: Quarry kid
replies.text: Three Pebblits, out and rolling. One rolled straight back to the quarry. Home is home.

stories.headline: Last crates stamped BRINEWICK. Great hustle!
body: The last crates at Bright Quarry are stamped BRINEWICK and ready to roll. Neat lettering, team.
Crates packed count toward Standing. Output and quotas, partners!

stories.headline: Hushwater: quiet stream, old weir, no stairs
body: Between the quarry and the glen runs Hushwater, a quiet stream that lives up to its name.
The Old Weir was built by Cobblecrest miners. The Fallstair says CLOSED FOR SURVEY. Sit by the weir instead.

stories.headline: Notice: a Keeper scout is on Hushwater
body: A Keeper scout is mapping the Hushwater stream for Captain Lumen. Please let the scout work.
The Captain's word: "The watch is mine. The town is the lantern's."

stories.headline: Mahopac, where the time is always now-ish
body: Mahopac's woods are time-snagged. Folk there, Nora, Cal and Bess, seem stuck in time. Time seems fine with it.
A line at Breckenridge Observatory reads: "The lens remembers." Nobody has argued.

stories.headline: The lens that remembers you better than you do
body: A lens at Breckenridge Observatory shows a holder three of their own memories.
A pop toy in 2004. A seventh birthday at a bowling alley. A drive-through with Dad.
"A Walkling trusts you faster once it has seen who you were."

replies.name: Lens visitor
replies.text: Saw my own childhood through the lens. The haircut was a choice. Not mine.

stories.headline: Dreams, noted: Warden Ilse keeps a ledger
body: Time is snagged in Mahopac, and the lens there shows memories. Somebody has to keep track.
Warden Ilse, at the Warden's Lodge, keeps a dream ledger. Sleep well. Dream kindly.

stories.headline: High Charity leaves the lights on
body: Step off the Lantern Coach into the Keeper capital. The house rule is short: be kind in the streets.
Sky-Dock Command, the Barracks, an Airship Field, a Canal Marina. Pace yourself. The lanterns aren't leaving.

replies.name: Coach rider
replies.text: My Walkling pressed its nose to the coach window the whole way in. Worth every smudge.

replies.name: Capital local
replies.text: Welcome! Yes, every roof. Yes, even that one. Please stop counting, it slows the street.

stories.headline: Event Hall: five games, six regulars, no mercy
body: The High Charity Event Hall runs five games, and Warden Ilse's invite gets you through the door.
The hall's six regulars swear they only play for fun. Watch their faces when you beat them.

replies.name: Event Hall regular
replies.text: Fun? Fun is for the other five games. This one is personal.

stories.headline: The Dojo: all of the sweat, none of the Seal
body: High Charity's Dojo is a practice hall, plain and simple. Holders come to practise, not to collect.
No Seal on the line. Seals still come from a Trial Hall, where a Master tests you. The eight are unchanged.

stories.headline: Porters Bram and Quin: mind the step
body: Porters Bram and Quin see holders onto the Lantern Coach, the way into the capital.
Their tip for new arrivals: lanterns on every roof, so look up. Be kind in the streets, so look out.

stories.headline: Ines keeps the capital's beds made
body: Host Ines runs the High Charity Lantern House: beds, a rest, and a plain word on how healing works.
A rest costs 5 Acorns. Short? Pay what you have. Empty pockets? It's free.
Beds don't cure Fade. Care does. Ines will say it twice if you need it twice.

stories.headline: Doorway, chair or exit: capital manners
body: A citizen waits in the doorway. A holder is offered a chair. A mint vest is asked to leave.
The Keepers are kind, the Post adds, and also watching. Sit up straight.

replies.name: Barracks neighbour
replies.text: Saw a mint vest get the polite version of 'out'. Very polite. Very out.

stories.headline: High Court: no holder goes without a phone
body: The Keeper High Court mandates a phone for every holder. Ribbit rides the Keeper wires.
Your Keeper1 is active. The Keepers can read it. That, the notice says, is the service.
Citizen. Say your piece, then step back.

replies.name: Route walker
replies.text: Free phone. Free feed. Free reading of my posts. Hello, Keepers. Lovely weather.

stories.headline: Lantern Council sits; a holder stands before it
body: The Lantern Council met in the Keeper capital, with a holder and their Seals before it.
The Keepers' word stands: walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them.
Feed, rest, listen, and leave glow where it grows.

replies.name: Lantern School pupil
replies.text: We copied the Keeper word into our books today. Neatest hand got the window seat. Not me.

replies.name: Barracks neighbour
replies.text: A holder walked out of that council with their chin up. Good sign, I reckon.

stories.headline: Lumen: 'The town is the lantern's'
body: Captain Lumen of Hearthmoor holds the Lantern Council in the Keeper capital.
'The watch is mine. The town is the lantern's.' The capital nodded along.

stories.headline: Signal Review: a bright quarter, says the screen
body: The Signal Review went over the relays. The Capital Partner joined by screen, as partners do.
'Policy is kindness, written down.' Have a bright day!
A cursor typed COUNT. GATHER. LISTEN. Head office has filed it under growth.

replies.name: Review attendee
replies.text: Someone read the cursor's last line out loud. It is not saying hello. Cool. Love that for us.

stories.headline: The associate who said it once, quietly
body: Associate Hollis ('I just hold the lamp') gave one holder a warning at the Signal Review.
'The lamps don't count glow. They count Walklings.' The desk prints it as heard, and leaves it there.

replies.name: Census walker
replies.text: Went back over my Census logs tonight. Counted something else this time.

stories.headline: Brighter by nature. Brighter by quarter.
body: Glimmerwell thanks every holder in the partnership. Units are cared for. Targets are quarterly.
Feeling low? Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting!

stories.headline: Guest today, Founder's Pick tomorrow?
body: Guest, Associate, Junior Bright, Bright Lead, Founder's Pick. Output and quotas move you up.
Junior Bright is Rook's level, so the bar is set. At the top, Marlowe knows your name.
It's a partnership!

replies.name: Lanyard wearer
replies.text: Marlowe knows your name at the top. I'd settle for my manager knowing it.

stories.headline: Route 3 opens, and the hum is 'normal'
body: The Brinewick road is open. Along it: a Comfort Sanctuary, a Shipping Ledger Office and a Relay House.
The Relay House has one line for visitors: 'The hum is normal.' Walkers have stopped asking twice.
Rook was at the Route 3 gate, waiting on a holder. Neighbour habits.

replies.name: Coast walker
replies.text: Long road. Good road. Weird hum. Three stars, would walk again.

stories.headline: Five on the Brinewick road answer the hum
body: Tallybat, Dimlamp, Filecrow, Cordhound, Humwisp. Ask anyone why and you get one line: 'The hum woke them.'
Keepers call them the Answerers. Glimmerwell calls them the Founder's Line. Same five either way.
They don't grow up. They rank Quiet, Humming, Answering.

replies.name: Lair spotter
replies.text: Met a Humming one. It looked at me like I was late for something.

stories.headline: One page in Mo's archive stays empty
body: Archivist Mo keeps a page on the five Walklings of the Brinewick road.
'The page on what they answer stays blank.' The Post leaves a little space blank beside it, too.

stories.headline: The Sanctuary has a room, not an address
body: Route 3 has a Comfort Sanctuary room. Crates of Walklings are bound for 'the Sanctuary'.
Where the crated Walklings go, nobody says. The memo does not ask, and hints that you shouldn't either.

replies.name: Ledger runner
replies.text: The Ledger Office has a lot of pages. None of them say where the Sanctuary is. I looked.

stories.headline: Brinewick: salt air, a ferry and a Tide Hall
body: A harbour town. Ferry at the west pier. A Trial Hall, a Lantern House, a Chandlery and a Glimmerwell Depot.
Master Marisol, the ferry captain, keeps the Tide Hall. Her advice to everyone: 'The tide's out. Sit a while.'

replies.name: Net mender
replies.text: New holders on the pier. Welcome. Benches are first come, first sit.

replies.name: Harbour hand
replies.text: Everyone asks where the ferry goes. The ferry asks where you've been. Sit a while.

stories.headline: A depot crate opens; a grey Drizzlet blinks out
body: A crate at the Brinewick depot held a Faded Drizzlet. A holder opened it.
Lantern Houses don't cure Fade. Care does, and the colour comes back: 'It remembers who it is.'

replies.name: Harbour hand
replies.text: Little grey thing blinked at the harbour like it forgot the sea. Give it time. Give it snacks.

replies.name: Pier walker
replies.text: Crates on our quay used to be furniture. Now I knock first.

stories.headline: Dorian Pell says 'units'; the quay winces
body: Dorian Pell, Glimmerwell's Head of Acquisitions, had his first battle at Brinewick, against a holder.
He calls Walklings 'units'. The harbour heard him say it, and harbours have long memories.

replies.name: Ferry rider
replies.text: My Walkling heard 'units' and turned its back on him. Good Walkling. Best Walkling.

stories.headline: Your Brinewick Depot: it's a partnership!
body: Glimmerwell's Brinewick Depot is proud to be part of the harbour, and the partnership. Brighter by nature.
Crates come and go. Questions can wait. Have a bright day!

stories.headline: Hall 3: Marisol hands over the Brinewick Seal
body: Master Marisol awarded the Brinewick Seal at the Tide Hall. Three Halls, three Seals.
The ferry captain's advice stands, win or lose: 'The tide's out. Sit a while.'

replies.name: Ferry rider
replies.text: Marisol battles like she sails. Calm, calm, calm, then very much not calm.

stories.headline: Quay review: one Tier 3 Lanyard, signed off
body: Dorian Pell reviewed a holder on the quay, and the Tier 3 Lanyard changed hands.
Master Marisol's match was optional. Output was not. Have a bright day!

replies.name: Pier walker
replies.text: Watched a review on our quay. Lots of nodding. Not one word about the tide.

stories.headline: Grey tower on the skyline; the clouds go flat
body: Holders report a grey tower. Above it, the clouds have gone flat, as if something pressed them.
The wire has nothing more on it yet. The desk is watching the sky. So should you.

replies.name: Harbour hand
replies.text: Clouds aren't meant to have corners. I'm just saying.

stories.headline: Wet grass, new noses on Route 1
body: Real rain on Route 1. The sky listens to the Far Sky, and today different Walklings stir in the grass.
Bring a hood. The tall grass will not dry off for you.

stories.headline: Night on the hill: the watch stays up
body: Hearthmoor watch, the lantern's law, works nights too. West watch is on the Plaza.
Let your Walkling sleep. Feed, rest, listen. The Keepers will do the staying up.

stories.headline: Snow on the hill: boots on, Walklings in
body: The Amberwild's sky listens to the Far Sky, and today it said snow. Hearthmoor's lanes have gone white.
Lantern House beds are warm. Not news, exactly, but nice to hear.

stories.headline: Dawn in the orchard: Pomlets first up
body: First light in Fernbrook. The Pomlets are already up and bothering the blossoms.
The Bloom Trial Hall is quiet. The orchard is not.

stories.headline: Grey sky, very bright lanterns
body: Overcast over Fernbrook. The free Glimmer lanterns look extra bright against it, which is surely the point.

stories.headline: Dusk on the ridge, wind in the tunnels
body: Fernbrook Heights after dark: a lab, old tunnels and a great deal of wind.
Walk the ridge with a friend and a Walkling. Ideally the Walkling knows the way.

stories.headline: Rain on Route 2. The puddles reopened too
body: Route 2's sky listens to the Far Sky, and today the Far Sky said rain. Walkers report damp socks.
Real weather changes which Walklings stir. Some love a puddle. Some sulk under a leaf.

stories.headline: Night under the Comfort Lamps: a slow pulse
body: After dark the Comfort Lamps of Wickerglen pulse like a slow heartbeat. Some walkers find it soothing.
Some count the beats. Some just walk a little faster.

stories.headline: Wickerglen after dark: no lamps, all snores
body: Night in Wickerglen since the lamps clicked off: just roots, and Walklings napping between them.
"Hush, please," says the sign. After dark it means it twice.

stories.headline: Snow on Cobblecrest; Pebblits unimpressed
body: Snow on the quarry town. Please mind the Pebblits underfoot, which are now also under snow.
Real weather changes which Walklings stir. The Pebblits have decided not to.

stories.headline: Sunny in Cobblecrest: warm stone, lazy Pebblits
body: Clear skies over the quarry town. Every warm stone has a Pebblit on it, or is one.
Please mind the Pebblits underfoot. Today they are not moving for anyone.

stories.headline: Dusk at the Old Weir: quiet, as advertised
body: Evening on Hushwater. The Old Weir, built by Cobblecrest miners, holds the stream the way it always has.
The Fallstair is still CLOSED FOR SURVEY. Sit, listen, and let the stream do the talking.

stories.headline: Dawn in Mahopac. Again? Possibly still
body: Morning came to Mahopac's time-snagged woods. Whether it is a new one is hard to say.
The observatory line holds: "The lens remembers." Somebody should.

stories.headline: Rain on the capital; every lantern holds
body: Rain over High Charity today, and every roof's lantern stayed lit through it.
Be kind in the streets still applies. The puddles count as streets.

stories.headline: Snow on every roof, a lantern on every roof
body: Snow settled over the Keeper capital. The lanterns on top didn't budge.
Canal Marina walkers report slippery going. Be kind in the streets, and slow.

stories.headline: After dark, the Barracks keep a light on
body: Night in High Charity is lanterns and quiet. The Keeper Barracks keep a light on regardless.
The Keepers are kind, and also awake.

stories.headline: Night walkers swear the hum gets louder
body: After dark on Route 3, walkers swear the hum carries further. The Relay House stands by 'The hum is normal.'
Lair spotters swear a Tallybat counted them as they passed. Unconfirmed. Possibly flattering.

stories.headline: Rain at the west pier; nobody on it minds
body: Rain over Brinewick. The ferry at the west pier is as wet as everyone else and twice as calm.
The Chandlery doorway is the driest spot in town. Form an orderly, damp line.

stories.headline: Dawn on the harbour: the tide's out, sit a while
body: Early light on Brinewick. Master Marisol's line fits the hour: 'The tide's out. Sit a while.'
The benches are damp. The day can wait.

stories.headline: Grey sky? That's just bad lighting!
body: Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting! The same goes for clouds.
Glimmerwell reminds every partner: brighter by nature, whatever the weather. Have a bright day!

stories.headline: Night shift: units rest, the quarter doesn't
body: Units rest. Targets are quarterly. Glimmerwell wishes every partner a quiet night.
Tier 2 partners: if your unit tilts its head at nothing tonight, that's just the quiet. Sleep well!

voices.text: Every new holder runs to the Lodge. Nobody walks to the Lodge. I have checked.
'A bond grows in small jobs.' Today's small job was finding my Walkling. Bond: strong.
My Walkling went GLOWING after a good day of care. I went GLOWING after a good lunch.
Turned up with zero Acorns once. Same bed, same blanket, same Della.
The Schoolhouse says Lanternball Court is a distraction. The Schoolhouse is wrong.
Said my piece. Stepped back. Felt extremely lawful for the rest of the day.
Up late. The watch walked by. I waved. The watch waved back, lawfully.
Rook took the starter that beats yours. He will tell you. He told me, and I was not even there.
Tall grass hides shy Walklings. It also hid my left shoe. Both are fine now.
Climbed a hill for better signal. Then remembered who owns the poles from this hill to the coast.
Rain day. Different Walklings out in the grass. My socks have made their peace with it.
Took a free lantern. Felt brighter by nature for about an hour. Then just felt like me.
A Pomlet sat in the basket I needed. Now I need a different basket.
Master Fen is out in the orchard again. The Hall is very tidy and very empty.
Somebody opened the crates at the gate. Associate Tobin reread the memo. Twice.
Quarterly targets are a team sport! Bring your own crate. Kidding! We bring the crates.
The old tunnels have the best echo on the ridge. Do not test this at night.
Saw the floating computer. It did not see me. I think. The screen was dark.
That census tent has more clipboards than I have socks. And I pack a lot of socks.
"Path reopened by Glimmerwell Co. crews!" The exclamation mark is theirs. The mud is mine.
Rain on Route 2 is the best rain. Ask any Walkling who just found a puddle.
Hush isn't a rule in Wickerglen. It's a personality.
"I just hold the lamp," he says. Sure. And I just stand near the snacks.
"Quarterly review, sweetie." She says it so sweetly. I have never been more nervous.
The lamps are off and the glen looks like itself again. I'd forgotten its real colour.
Tiptoed through the glen at night. Something snored. Hoping it was a Walkling.
Rule one in Cobblecrest: look down. Rule two: that's a Pebblit. Rule three: say sorry.
Hale says forty years he dug beside Walklings. Looks like he's got forty more in him.
Fair and square, the Reeve says. Square, sure. Fair, I'm still chewing on.
The desk at Bright Quarry is very clean. Clerk Mint is very polite. The stone is still stone.
Cobblecrest miners built the Old Weir. Gran says it is the only thing in town that never complains.
Hale opened the seam again. The whole quarry sounds like a lazy afternoon.
Stamped BRINEWICK so many times today I'm signing my letters with it.
Asked what year it is. Got a smile and a shrug. Mahopac's like that.
Looked through the lens expecting stars. Got my own childhood instead. Rude, but fair.
"Eat up. The world can wait." Best advice in the woods, and it came from a dream.
Every roof, every night. Visitors ask if the lanterns get tired. Do you?
The marina Walklings know which bench is mine. They sit on it first. On purpose.
Six of us. Five games. One rule: nobody touches my high score.
First lesson: be kind in the streets. Then fractions. Kindness was easier.
No Seal on the line here, so nobody cries. Well. Less crying.
A Walkling tried to deposit a leaf. The queue voted to let it. The queue was overruled.
Ribbit rides our wires. Post nicely. We read it all, but we like the nice ones best.
Citizen. Say your piece, then step back. Then maybe one more step. Thank you.
Mint vest, mandatory smile, quarterly target. Have a bright day! I mean it. I have to.
My partner stares at the ceiling sometimes, like it heard a phone ring. Nothing rang.
The hum is normal. I hummed back once. Nothing happened. Should something have happened?
The Shipping Ledger Office has more pages than this road has steps. I'd know. I walk both.
Saw a Quiet one. Took one step closer. It went Humming. I took two steps back.
Rain on the Brinewick road, and the hum doesn't stop for it. Neither do we. Walkling under my coat.
The tide's out. Sit a while. Captain's orders, more or less.
Came in for rope. Left with rope and a Walkling asleep in my bag. Good trade.
Our Lantern Host still has no name tag. Heals you anyway. Explains it slower than the tide.
Since the crate business, I knock on every depot crate I pass. Just in case.
Night on the west pier. Water slapping, lanterns low, one Walkling snoring on a rope coil.
The clouds over that grey tower look ironed. I don't trust ironed clouds.

notices.title: LANTERN HOUSE: REST UP
notices.text: Hurt or tired? Della has beds. 5 Acorns, or what you have, or free at 0.

notices.title: FROM KEEPER HOUSE
notices.text: Walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them. Feed, rest, listen. Thank you, citizen.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE SCARF
notices.text: Left by Lanternball Court. Smells strongly of Walkling. Ask at Keeper House.

notices.title: SEEN: ONE SLEEPY WALKLING
notices.text: Napping on Market Row since breakfast. Not lost. Just very comfortable. Let it be.

notices.title: KEEPER1: CARRY IT
notices.text: Every holder must carry a free Keeper1. Officer Ness issues them on Route 1.

notices.title: LOST: ONE BALL
notices.text: Last seen rolling into the tall grass. A shy Walkling may be keeping it. Let it.

notices.title: ON FADE
notices.text: Lantern Houses do not cure Fade. Care does. Keeper Amos will explain, kindly.

notices.title: BLOOM TRIAL HALL
notices.text: Master Fen tests holders for a Seal. If the Hall is empty, try the orchard.

notices.title: KEEPER STANDING
notices.text: Care and kindness earn Standing. Trusted holders find a Lantern House bed saved.

notices.title: FREE GLIMMER LANTERNS
notices.text: Brighter by nature! Free lanterns at the Fernbrook stand. It's a partnership!

notices.title: FEELING TIRED?
notices.text: Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting! Ask a mint vest. Have a bright day!

notices.title: CLIMB THE TIERS
notices.text: Guest, Associate, Junior Bright, Bright Lead. Your next tier is one quota away!

notices.title: HEIGHTS: TUNNELS QUIET
notices.text: The night crates are open and the old tunnels are quiet. Leave a light. Leave them wild.

notices.title: ROUTE 2: WALK BESIDE
notices.text: Walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them. Feed, rest, listen. The Keepers.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE MITTEN
notices.text: Left on a flat stone by the Route 2 path. Damp but cheerful. Its twin is out there.

notices.title: COUNT WITH THE CENSUS
notices.text: Every Census log counts toward Standing. Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting!

notices.title: HUSH, PLEASE
notices.text: Walklings nap here between the roots. Whisper, tiptoe, and keep your snack wrappers quiet.

notices.title: SEEN: ONE SLEEPY WALKLING
notices.text: Napping between the roots in Wickerglen. Not lost. Just busy. Please do not wake.

notices.title: LANTERN HOUSE: BEDS READY
notices.text: Garnet keeps the beds in Cobblecrest. A rest is 5 Acorns; with none at all, it's free.

notices.title: BRINEWICK ROAD CLOSED
notices.text: Closed while crates are loaded. The Keepers ask: mind the Pebblits underfoot either way.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE DUSTY GLOVE
notices.text: Found by the quarry path. Smells of stone. A Pebblit has been guarding it. Ask nicely.

notices.title: BRIGHT QUARRY IS OPEN
notices.text: A Glimmerwell Co. site. Clerk Mint is at the desk. It's a partnership! Have a bright day!

notices.title: FALLSTAIR: CLOSED
notices.text: CLOSED FOR SURVEY, says the sign at Hushwater. The Old Weir is still fine for sitting.

notices.title: MAHOPAC: TIME SNAGS
notices.text: Time-snagged woods. If the day feels familiar, it is. Keep your Walkling close.

notices.title: LOST: THE TIME
notices.text: Last seen in Mahopac's woods. Nora, Cal and Bess may have it. Or had it. Hard to say.

notices.title: BRIGHTER BY NATURE
notices.text: Glimmer lanterns: free, friendly, always on. Why sit in the dark? Brighter by nature.

notices.title: IT'S A PARTNERSHIP!
notices.text: Your Walkling is a unit. You are a partner. Together, you're a quarterly target!

notices.title: FEELING TIRED?
notices.text: Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting! Ask any mint vest about Comfort Lamps.

notices.title: CLIMB THE TIERS
notices.text: Guest to Founder's Pick, one quota at a time. Marlowe knows the names at the top.

notices.title: TIER 2? STAY BRIGHT
notices.text: Tier 2 units may feel a soft click of belonging. Totally normal. Have a bright day!

notices.title: YOUR BRINEWICK DEPOT
notices.text: Crates in, crates out, smiles all round. Your harbour depot. It's a partnership!

notices.title: COMFORT SANCTUARY
notices.text: Somewhere restful for every crated unit. Where, exactly? That's the restful part.

notices.title: NOW IN THE CAPITAL
notices.text: Mint vests may be asked to leave. Bright ideas never are. Have a bright day!

notices.title: LANTERN COACH
notices.text: Porters Bram and Quin will see you aboard. Be kind in the streets, and in the queue.

notices.title: CAPITAL LANTERN HOUSE
notices.text: Host Ines keeps beds ready. Rest is 5 Acorns, or what you have. Fade needs care.

notices.title: KEEPER1 REMINDER
notices.text: Your Keeper1 is active. We can read this. That is the service. Leave a light.

notices.title: WALK SOFT ON ROUTE 3
notices.text: Five Walklings answer the hum here. Walk beside them, not ahead of them.

notices.title: TIDE HALL
notices.text: Master Marisol keeps the Tide Hall and the ferry both. If she's out, sit a while.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE SANDY SCARF
notices.text: Left on a bench by the west pier. Smells of salt. Ask at the Lantern House.

notices.title: SEEN NAPPING
notices.text: One sleepy Walkling, curled on a Canal Marina bench. Not lost, it says. Just resting.

notices.title: LOST: ONE SANDAL
notices.text: Somewhere on the Brinewick road. If a Walkling is chewing it, it may keep it.

polls.q: Best nap spot for a Walkling?
Which first Walkling would you pick?
Your Keeper1 can read this. Feelings?
Best nap spot for a Pebblit?
The quarry vote: how would you have voted?
The lens shows one memory. Which first?
Best name on the Brinewick road?

you.headline: {holder} and {partner}, out walking
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. Old Meadow sends its regards.
The paper notes no complaints from the grass.

you.headline: {town} has new regulars
body: Folks in {town} say {holder} and {partner} are part of the scenery now. The good part.

you.headline: {partner} looks happy, sources say
body: Keep {partner}'s care at 75 or more and the GLOWING mood shows. Sources say {holder} knows the trick.

you.headline: Market Row has noticed {holder}
body: Word on Market Row: {holder} has Acorns in pocket. Lamplight Provisions is trying to look casual.

you.headline: Seal count for {holder}: {seals}
body: Seals so far for {holder}: {seals}. The level cap climbs with every one.
{partner} has been told. {partner} is very proud.

you.headline: {holder} takes Route 2 at a stroll
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. The Route 2 gravel has filed no complaints.

you.headline: {partner} keeps the hush in Wickerglen
body: Spotted: {holder} and {partner} tiptoeing between the roots. Nobody woke. The paper approves.

you.headline: {seals} Seals and counting for {holder}
body: Master Hale's Stone Hall saw {holder} and {partner} at work. The Pebblits rolled over in respect.
More Seals, higher level cap. Hale nodded, which for Hale is a standing ovation.

you.headline: {town} has a bed for {holder}
body: {holder} has the Acorns for a Lantern House bed, and {partner} has the yawn. Sounds like a plan.

you.headline: {holder} visits Mahopac. Or did. Or will
body: Time snags in Mahopac's woods. {partner} stuck close to {holder} the whole time, whichever time it was.

you.headline: {holder} rolls into the capital
body: {holder} stepped off the Lantern Coach into High Charity. The lanterns on every roof did not comment.

you.headline: Seen in {town}: {holder}
body: The Keeper wires noticed {holder} in {town} today. Kind in the streets? The Keepers think so.
Your Keeper1 is active. That is the service.

you.headline: {holder} and {partner} sit a while
body: The tide's out at Brinewick, and {holder} and {partner} took the advice. {seals} Seals, zero hurry.

you.headline: {partner} out-walks the Brinewick road
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. Route 3 is long, and {partner} wants every step.

you.headline: Partner of the quarter: {holder}?
body: {holder} and unit {partner} are trending toward target. Glimmerwell is so proud. Have a bright day!
